Judgment

Suit is one for permanent injunction to restrain the defendant from proceeding against the schedule site property in furtherance of E-auction notification dated 22.02.2015 published in daily newspapers and for consequential relief of permanent injunction to restrain the defendant from interfering with the possession of the plaintiff.

2. Case of the plaintiff in brief is as here under:-
The plaintiff is the absolute owner in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property having purchased the same under registered sale deed dated 19.01.2005 from Mr. Mohammed Pyare Jan and Sri. M.Kuppuswamy for valuable consideration of Rs.7,90,000/-.

Since the date of purchase, the plaintiff is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property and khata is transferred to his name and he is regularly paying taxes to the concerned authority.

The plaintiff dug bore-well in the suit property on 03.02.2005 and got approved plan and sketch from CMC,
Bytarayanapura on 22.02.2005 and also got electricity connection transferred to his name and started construction of building.

It is stated that the adjacent owner on the northern side caused obstruction to the construction work, disputing the boundary line between the sites and he filed O.S. No.16323/2005 seeking relief of injunction and this plaintiff also filed O.S. No.3420/2005 and both the suits are pending before the Court at Mayohall.
The vendors of the plaintiff Sri. Mohammed Pyare Jan and M.Kuppuswamy had purchased the property from one R.Srinivasan under sale deed dated 18.05.2005 and vide rectification deed dated 05.06.2007.

It is stated that on 09.03.2015, the plaintiff came to know that the defendant has shown the suit schedule property as one of 71 items of sites i.e. item No.36 in the E-auction notification published in Kannada and English newspaper dated 22.02.2015 with sketch inviting the general public to participate in the auction sale.
The properties of the defendants starts from site No.672.
But the defendant has included site No.671 which belongs to the plaintiff.
Hence, the plaintiff immediately approached the defendant authorities and submitted requisition along with all the documents standing in his name.

The defendant assured to take note of his representation Narasimhan C vs Bangalore Development Authority on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34261041/
2 assuring that if it is not acquired by B.D.A. they will stop the sale proceedings.

sentences.text: But in spite of repeated visits to the defendant office and enquiries made, they did not disclose any such attempts as assured.
Hence, it is apprehension of the plaintiff that the defendant may proceed further in the said auction process.

It is stated that the suit property and the adjoining 3 sites comprising 10 guntas of land were not acquired by the defendant and the remaining 3 sites, the owner and other purchasers have already constructed their buildings and have been enjoying their own properties.

if the defendant is not restrained from proceeding further in the E-auction proceeding, the plaintiff will suffer loss and injury and hence, the cause of action to file the suit arose and hence, the suit.
3.

In pursuance to the summons issued the defendant B.D.A. caused appearance and filed written statement wherein which it is stated that the defendant has acquired the suit schedule land under notification published in the official Gazette and hence in view of the acquisition, the present suit is not maintainable and is liable dismissed.

It is stated that this defendant acquired agricultural property in Sy. No.219 of Kachakarakanahalli village measuring 1 acre 20 guntas from its khathedars Sri. Patil B. Adaviappa, Sri. C.V.Ramachandra, Smt. Puttagangamma and Sri.
H.Hanumareddy

vide preliminary notification No.BDA/ALAO/S/11/78-79 dated 27.06.1978 and final notification No.HUD.567-MNX-84 dated 09.01.1985, possession was taken on 24.07.1985 and award dated 14.08.1986 and the same was entrusted to the Engineering Department for formation of HBR Layout.
Further Sri. Mohammed Pyare Jan and M.Kuppuswamy had no right, title or interest over the schedule property to execute the sale deed in favour of the plaintiff.
As such, the plaintiff has no right, title or interest over the schedule property and the plaintiff at no point of time was in possession of the suit schedule property.

Since the property has been acquired by this defendant, the CMC Byatarayanapura or B.B.M.P. has no jurisdiction to collect the taxes and to issue khata in favour of the plaintiff and as such, khata issued by the B.B.M.P. or CMC have no sanctity in the eye of law and is not binding on this defendant.

This defendant B.D.A. being the owner of the property by virtue of acquisition has issued E-auction notification in the daily newspapers and it is the defendant which is in possession of the schedule property.

Since the plaintiff is neither the owner nor in possession of the schedule property, the plaintiff is not entitled for the relief claimed and the plaintiff has not issued any notice under Sec.64 of the B.D.A. Act and hence, the suit against this defendant is not maintainable and contending these facts sought for dismissal of suit.
4. Heard learned counsel for defendant and in the absence of representation for plaintiff, this Court could not have the benefit of hearing the arguments of the plaintiff.
5. The aforesaid pleadings have occasioned following:-
ISSUES 1.
Whether the plaintiff proves that defendant has put suit property for auction illegally ?

3. Whether suit of the plaintiff is maintainable ?
4. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief sought ?
5. What order or decree ?
6. In order to discharge the burden, the plaintiff got examined himself as P.W.1 and he has relied upon 49 documents marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.49 and closed the evidence.
7. Per contra, the First Division Assistant of defendant B.D.A. got examined himself as D.W.1 and relied upon 6 documents marked at Ex.D.1 to Ex.D.6 and closed the evidence.
8. My findings to the above issues are as follows:

ISSUE No.1 :: In the Negative ISSUE No.2 :: In the Negative ISSUE No.3 :: In the Negative ISSUE No.4 :: In the Negative ISSUE No.5 :: As per final order for the following;
REASONS 9. ISSUES NO.1 TO 4 :: All these issues are taken up collectively for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts and also for convenience of the Court.

The present suit is filed by the plaintiff as against B.D.A. for the relief of permanent injunction to restrain the defendant and its men from proceeding against the schedule site property in furtherance of E-auction notification dated 22.02.2015 published in two English and Kannada daily newspapers and also to restrain the defendant from interfering with the possession of the plaintiff during pendency of the suit.

The description of the schedule property involved in the present suit is as hereunder:-
SCHEDULE The immovable property bearing House list No.2353/3, (bearing old Khata No.3687) presently bearing H.L.No.2383/2, CMC Khata No.225, situated at Kacharakanahalli Village, Kasaba Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru measuring East to West - 60 ft. and North to South - 40 ft. actually measuring East to West - 63 ft. and North to South - 40 ft. totally measuring 2520 sq. ft. together with a AC sheet house measuring 1 square and bounded by:

10. The plaintiff in order to prove that, without there being acquisition of the suit site,
the defendant has illegally subjected the suit schedule property for public auction got examined himself as P.W.1 and he has in his evidence deposed that he is the absolute owner in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule site having purchased the same under sale deed dated 19.01.2005 from its erstwhile owner Mr. Mohammed Pyare Jan and Sri. N.Kuppuswamy for consideration of Rs.7,90,000/-.
It is stated that the vendor of the plaintiff had purchased the suit schedule property by obtaining no objection certificate from the defendant.

Later, the plaintiff got transferred khata to his name at CMC Byatarayanapura and in view of amalgamation of CMC with B.B.M.P., the records continued in the name of plaintiff in the B.B.M.P. records and since then plaintiff is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule site and in order to put up construction of residential house he has dug bore- well and got approved the plan and sketch from concerned authority on 22.02.2005 and also got obtained electricity connection in the month of March 2005 and started construction of the building as per the sanctioned plan.

He has deposed that his vendors had purchased the site from its owner Sri. R.Srinivasan under sale deed dated 18.05.2005 and since there was mistake crept with regard to the house list number a rectification deed dated 05.06.2007 was executed in between them. P.W.1 has deposed that the defendant has issued public notice in respect of 71 sites for E- auction in newspapers on 22.02.2015 inviting the general public to participate in the auction sale.
It is his contention that the site of the defendant starts from site No.672, but the defendant has included his site bearing No.671 which is the schedule site in the publication.

Immediately he approached the defendant authorities and they assured that the site is not acquired and as such they will stop the sale proceedings, but in spite of it, they did not take any positive action.

Since the defendant has not acquired the adjoining 3 sites in respect of the suit schedule property which comprises 10 guntas of land and in the remaining 3 sites the owner and purchasers have already constructed buildings and are enjoying the same as absolute owners thereof and since there was repeated attempts by the defendant to interfere with his possession and made attempts to proceed with E-auction proceeding,
the suit is filed.

11. In order to establish the flow of title and the possession of plaintiff over the suit schedule site,
P.W.1 has produced Ex.P.27 which is the original sale deed dated 05.08.1991 which shows one G.N.Prahlada and Sri. Abdul Razak as vendors have sold the site bearing house list No.2353/3 measuring East to West 60 ft. and North to South 40 ft. which comprises 1 square house constructed thereon in favour of Sri. R.Srinivasan.
The recitals of this document nowhere shows how the said vendors acquired right over the suit schedule site.

Be that as it may, Ex.P.29 is the rectification deed dated 10.12.2004 which shows the said deed is executed between the same vendors and R.Srinivasan and it shows the name of the vendor Sri. K.M.Chikka Chowdappa S/o. Sri.
Munivenkatappa is included as vendor and the said Prahlada and Abdul Razak are shown to be the G.P.A. holders of Chikka Chowdappa and this is the rectification done in the said rectification deed.

Ex.P.26 and Ex.P.31 are the rectification deeds dated 05.06.2007 which shows rectification is done in respect of the property number and the house list No.2353/3 is rectified as 2353/2 measuring East to West 60 ft. and North to South 40 ft. actually measuring East to West 63 ft. and North to South 40 ft.

Ex.P.14 is the sale deed of the plaintiff dated 19.01.2005 which shows the said Mr.
Mohammed Pyare Jan and Kuppuswamy have sold the suit schedule site in favour of the plaintiff and the recitals of the said documents shows that the suit schedule site was originally owned by Sri.
K.M.Chikka Chowdappa and he subsequently sold the same in favour of the Prahlada and Abdul Razak by executing G.P.A. dated 20.06.1984 and executed affidavit confirming the same and later,
the said purchasers sold site No.2353/2 in favour of Srinivasan who in turn sold the property in favour of the vendors of the plaintiff.

So these documents establishes that suit schedule site is sold under various sale deeds and finally under Ex.P.14 the plaintiff has purchased the suit schedule site and description of the suit site tallies with the sale deed placed on record.
13.

Further in order to establish his possession, P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P.1 which is the endorsement issued by B.D.A. on 21.01.2004 in favour of the erstwhile owner Srinivasan wherein which he has sought details about the acquisition of the land in Sy. No.219 of Kacharakanahalli village in respect of house list 2353/2 and in this regard B.D.A. has endorsed that Sy. No.219 is acquired by B.D.A. for formation of HBR 1st Stage layout and house list No.2353/2 comprises structure and no objection certificate is issued.

Further, Ex.P.2 shows the plaintiff herein has filed the said suit as against one Smt. Gayathridevi and Imran seeking relief of permanent injunction in respect of the suit schedule site and it is stated that he is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property and when he made attempts to put up construction interference was caused by the defendants and hence, the suit is filed.

Ex.P.3 is the E-auction notification issued in the daily newspaper by B.D.A. which shows the various sites are subjected to E-auction and this public notice nowhere shows the suit schedule site bearing No.2353/3 is subjected to E-auction.

Ex.P.4 to Ex.P.6 are the various representations given by the plaintiff to the various authorities i.e. B.D.A. and Land Acquisition Officer wherein which he has requested the authority to not to proceed with the E-auction proceeding.
Ex . P.7 to Ex.P.13 are the photos and CD to show the existing condition of the suit schedule site.

Further, P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P.15 to Ex.P.18 which are the tax paid receipts,
khata certificate and sanction plan which shows the suit schedule site stands in the name of plaintiff and khata is effected in his name in the year 2008 and he has obtained plan from B.D.A. for construction house.
Ex . P.20
and Ex

Ex.P.36 and Ex.P.37 shows the plaintiff has applied before the land acquisition officer under the Right to Information Act seeking information about the acquisition of the land bearing Sy. No.219 and it is informed to the plaintiff that Sy. No.219 measuring 1 acre 12 guntas is acquired and Narasimhan C vs Bangalore Development Authority on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34261041/
6 compensation amount is deposited before the City Civil Court and this endorsement is supported by the preliminary notification and final notification placed on record which shows Sy. No.219 measuring 1 acre 12 guntas is acquired and compensation is deposited before the Civil Court.

sentences.text:
But Ex.P.38 to Ex.P.41 which are the assessment list and demand register extract pertaining to Sy.
No.219 for the year 2004-05, 2003-04 and 1991-92 shows the property originally stood in the name of Srinivasan and later it stands in the name of plaintiff.
Further, in order to prove that the adjacent sites are not acquired and it is owned by the owners.

P.W.1 has produced Ex.P.45 which is the sale deed dated 19.02.2005 which shows house list No.2353/1 was sold in favour of one Mr. A.Aejaz Ali by Mr. A.Syed Hamid Ahmed and that he is in possession of the said site.
14. During his cross-examination he admits schedule property is carved out in Sy. No.219 of Kacharakanahalli village and he has not mentioned the survey number in the plaint schedule.

He also admits that Sy. No.219 is acquired by B.D.A. and also admits that the B.D.A. had informed him about acquisition proceedings during 1978-86 and he also admits that site No.671 was subjected to E-auction and it is situated at 3rd Block, 1st Stage, HBR Layout and HBR Layout is formed by B.D.A.

He also admits that Sy. No.672 is situated adjacent to schedule property and on enquiry with B.D.A.
of officials, he came to know that B.D.A. formed HBR Layout upto site No.672.
P.W.1 says he has not produced any document to show who has formed the layout of schedule property.
The suggestion putforth that his vendors had no right over the schedule property and neither himself nor his vendors are in possession of the schedule property
are all denied by P.W.1.
So there is a clear admission by P.W.1 that site No.671 was put to E-auction and site No.672 is adjacent to the said site.

15. But it is necessary to take note of the fact that the evidence of P.W.1 and the documents relied upon by him shows that he has purchased the suit schedule property and all the documents stands in the name of plaintiff.

But the plaintiff has in his evidence deposed that the B.D.A. has published in the daily newspapers regarding sale of 71 sites in the E-auction and according to the plaintiff, site No.671 is included in the list of sites though the site of the defendants starts from site No.672.
So this evidence of P.W.1 is totally inconsistent with each other.

When the plaintiff claims to be in possession and enjoyment of the property bearing house list No.2353/2 and all the documents produced by him corroborates the same, his claim that he is in possession of site No.671 and the said site do not belong to the B.D.A. is not tenable.
P.W.1 has failed to establish before the Court as to whether he is asserting right over site No.671 or the suit schedule property and his evidence is totally inconsistent in this regard.

Further admission of P.W.1 clearly shows that site No.671 belongs to B.D.A. and it was subjected to E-auction and also there is a clear admission that the said site comes within the property acquired by B.D.A. and the layout formed by B.D.A.

So under such circumstances, the evidence of plaintiff that he is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property which is site No.671 and it is shown as item No.36 in the list of sites subjected to E-auction holds no substance.

16. On the contrary, the defendant got examined through its official as D.W.1 and he has in his evidence deposed that the defendant authority has acquired agricultural land bearing Sy. No.219 of Kacharakanahalli village measuring 1 acre 20 guntas from its khathedars i.e. Sri. Patil B. Adaviappa,
C.V.Ramachandra, Smt. Puttagangamma and Sri. Hanumareddy under vide preliminary notification No.BDA/ALAO/S/11/78-79 dated 27.06.1978 and final notification No.HUD.567-MNX-84 dated Narasimhan C vs Bangalore Development Authority on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34261041/
7 09.01.1985, possession was taken on 24.07.1985 and award dated 14.08.1986 under Section 16(2)
published on 15.05.1987.
Further the land was entrusted to the Engineering Department for formation of HBR Layout and layout has been formed.
It is stated that the said Sri. Md. Pyare Jan and Kuppuswamy had no right, title or interest over the schedule property to execute sale deed in favour of the plaintiff.

As such, the plaintiff has no right, title or interest over the schedule property and at no point of time the plaintiff was in possession and all documents produced by the plaintiff are concocted documents in order to knock off the property of the defendant.

It is stated that on 18.02.2015 the B.D.A. has given E-auction notification to auction sites belonging to B.D.A. as per the notification including site No.671, situated at 1st Stage, 3rd Block, HBR Layout and the B.D.A. has every right to issue E-auction notification as the B.D.A. is the owner of the property by virtue of acquisition.

The authority has not issue notification in respect of site No.2353/3 or 2383/2 and the plaintiff is not in possession of suit property at any point of time and it is fake site numbers and the plaintiff is claiming right over site No.671 and hence is false suit filed with an intention to knock off the public property by misleading this Court and since the B.D.A. is the owner in possession of site No.671, the suit is not maintainable and sought for dismissal of suit.

17. In support of of his evidence he has produced Ex.D.1 to Ex.D.5 which are the preliminary notification, final notification which shows Sy. No.219 measuring 1 acre 12 guntas is acquired and the khathedars are shown as Sri. Patil B. Adviappa, C.V.Ramachandra, Smt. Puttagangamma and Sri. Hanumareddy and award is passed and compensation amount is deposited before the Civil Court.
But it is worth to note that the plaintiff has not chosen to cross- examination D.W.1.
So by this the evidence of D.W.1 has remained unchallenged.

So these documents relied upon by the defendant shows that Sy. No.219 measuring 1 acre 12 guntas situated at Kacharakanahalli village is acquired by B.D.A. and has formed HBR Layout and various sites are formed and the B.D.A. has issued E-auction notification in the daily newspaper for the sale of sites.

Further the admission of P.W.1 makes it clear that site No.671 over which the plaintiff is asserting right belongs to B.D.A. and as such, the B.D.A. being the owner in possession of site No.671 along with other sites has put the sites for auction.
Further as stated earlier, the evidence of plaintiff is inconsistent as to his possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule property.
P.W.1 at one point of time states that he is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property and all the documents are produced by him to show his possession over the said property.

But in his evidence he is asserting right over site No.671 and no evidence is forthcoming as to how he has acquired right over site No.671 and as to where the property is situated and there is no evidence forthcoming to show that the suit schedule property is renumbered as site No.671.

So the plaintiff has though established that he is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property, his evidence that he is in possession of site No.671 and B.D.A. has illegally subjected the said property for sale holds no substance and the plaintiff has failed to establish his right over site No.671.
Hence, the plaintiff is not entitled for the relief claimed.
Accordingly, this Court proceeds to answer the aforesaid issues No.1 to 4 in the Negative.
18. ISSUE NO.5 ::

In view of findings given on Issues No.1 to 4, this Court proceeds to pass the following;
ORDER Suit of the plaintiff is dismissed.

Suit is one for permanent injunction to restrain the defendant from proceeding against the schedule site property in furtherance of E-auction notification dated 22.02.2015 published in daily newspapers and for consequential relief of permanent injunction to restrain the defendant from interfering with the possession of the plaintiff.
Since the date of purchase, the plaintiff is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property and khata is transferred to his name and he is regularly paying taxes to the concerned authority.
The vendors of the plaintiff Sri. Mohammed Pyare Jan and M.Kuppuswamy had purchased the property from one R.Srinivasan under sale deed dated 18.05.2005 and vide rectification deed dated 05.06.2007.
Further Sri. Mohammed Pyare Jan and M.Kuppuswamy had no right, title or interest over the schedule property to execute the sale deed in favour of the plaintiff.
As such, the plaintiff has no right, title or interest over the schedule property and the plaintiff at no point of time was in possession of the suit schedule property.
Since the property has been acquired by this defendant, the CMC Byatarayanapura or B.B.M.P. has no jurisdiction to collect the taxes and to issue khata in favour of the plaintiff and as such, khata issued by the B.B.M.P. or CMC have no sanctity in the eye of law and is not binding on this defendant.
This defendant B.D.A. being the owner of the property by virtue of acquisition has issued E-auction notification in the daily newspapers and it is the defendant which is in possession of the schedule property.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The present suit is filed by the plaintiff as against B.D.A. for the relief of permanent injunction to restrain the defendant and its men from proceeding against the schedule site property in furtherance of E-auction notification dated 22.02.2015 published in two English and Kannada daily newspapers and also to restrain the defendant from interfering with the possession of the plaintiff during pendency of the suit.
10. The plaintiff in order to prove that, without there being acquisition of the suit site,
the defendant has illegally subjected the suit schedule property for public auction got examined himself as P.W.1 and he has in his evidence deposed that he is the absolute owner in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule site having purchased the same under sale deed dated 19.01.2005 from its erstwhile owner Mr. Mohammed Pyare Jan and Sri. N.Kuppuswamy for consideration of Rs.7,90,000/-.
So this evidence of P.W.1 is totally inconsistent with each other.
When the plaintiff claims to be in possession and enjoyment of the property bearing house list No.2353/2 and all the documents produced by him corroborates the same, his claim that he is in possession of site No.671 and the said site do not belong to the B.D.A. is not tenable.
P.W.1 has failed to establish before the Court as to whether he is asserting right over site No.671 or the suit schedule property and his evidence is totally inconsistent in this regard.
Further admission of P.W.1 clearly shows that site No.671 belongs to B.D.A. and it was subjected to E-auction and also there is a clear admission that the said site comes within the property acquired by B.D.A. and the layout formed by B.D.A.
So under such circumstances, the evidence of plaintiff that he is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property which is site No.671 and it is shown as item No.36 in the list of sites subjected to E-auction holds no substance.
The authority has not issue notification in respect of site No.2353/3 or 2383/2 and the plaintiff is not in possession of suit property at any point of time and it is fake site numbers and the plaintiff is claiming right over site No.671 and hence is false suit filed with an intention to knock off the public property by misleading this Court and since the B.D.A. is the owner in possession of site No.671, the suit is not maintainable and sought for dismissal of suit.
Further the admission of P.W.1 makes it clear that site No.671 over which the plaintiff is asserting right belongs to B.D.A. and as such, the B.D.A. being the owner in possession of site No.671 along with other sites has put the sites for auction.
But in his evidence he is asserting right over site No.671 and no evidence is forthcoming as to how he has acquired right over site No.671 and as to where the property is situated and there is no evidence forthcoming to show that the suit schedule property is renumbered as site No.671.
So the plaintiff has though established that he is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property, his evidence that he is in possession of site No.671 and B.D.A. has illegally subjected the said property for sale holds no substance and the plaintiff has failed to establish his right over site No.671.
Hence, the plaintiff is not entitled for the relief claimed.

ORDER Suit of the plaintiff is dismissed.
